summary: Depth-first rabbithole dossier for Deferring Maintenance; source-anchored research pack.

facts.text: [medium] The 'Automatically defer maintenance for one week' option causes Atlas to defer future scheduled maintenance by one week each time, resulting in maintenance running every two weeks. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/cluster-maintenance-window.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/configure-maintenance-window-settings.md

The Terraform/Pulumi maintenance window attribute 'defer' defers the next scheduled maintenance event by one week, but only works when maintenance is already scheduled. The corresponding Atlas CLI command is 'atlas maintenanceWindows defer', which defers scheduled maintenance for a project for one week. Sources: https://www.pulumi.com/registry/packages/mongodbatlas/api-docs/maintenancewindow/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/command/atlas-maintenanceWindows-defer.md

[high] The auto_defer_once_enabled attribute enables automatic deferral of all scheduled maintenance for the project by one week. An issue reporter in terraform-provider-mongodbatlas issue #3155 suggested this would also defer urgent security patches, but Atlas documentation says urgent maintenance such as security patches cannot wait for the chosen window. Sources: https://github.com/mongodb/terraform-provider-mongodbatlas/issues/3155, https://www.pulumi.com/registry/packages/mongodbatlas/api-docs/maintenancewindow/

[low] Atlas allows users to defer scheduled maintenance for one week or begin it immediately, with a banner displayed 48-72 hours prior and email notifications sent to Project Owners. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/respond-to-required-maintenance.md

[medium] Automatic deferral of maintenance is unavailable for projects in an organization if any project within that organization has a maintenance wave configured. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/cluster-maintenance-window.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/configure-maintenance-window-settings.md

[medium] Manual deferral of maintenance is restricted to projects with a maintenance wave configured only if they are assigned to Last Wave, and these projects are limited to at most one manual deferral. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/cluster-maintenance-window.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/respond-to-required-maintenance.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/configure-maintenance-window-settings.md

[high] A single project maintenance event can be deferred up to two times, with the deferral count tracking how many times the current event has been postponed. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/respond-to-required-maintenance.md, https://www.pulumi.com/registry/packages/mongodbatlas/api-docs/maintenancewindow/

'auto_defer' is a Terraform provider attribute of mongodbatlas_maintenance_window that defers any scheduled maintenance for the project for one week; it makes a one-time call to the Atlas toggleMaintenanceAutoDefer endpoint (CLI equivalent: 'atlas api maintenanceWindows toggleMaintenanceAutoDefer'). Sources: https://github.com/mongodb/terraform-provider-mongodbatlas/issues/3155 ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/command/atlas-api-maintenanceWindows-toggleMaintenanceAutoDefer.md

[low] Users should allow all deferred maintenance to complete to ensure their clusters are on the latest versions. Sources: https://intercom-help.mongodb.com/en/articles/16063007-july-2026-security-release
